clue.text: In what way? A way shown by the Admiral

parts.note: the question 'in what way?' is simply 'how?'
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A naval quiz: someone asks which route the Admiral pointed out.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Howard of Effingham was the English Lord High Admiral who commanded against the Spanish Armada in 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Howard was the famous Elizabethan naval commander, so a well-known Admiral by surname.

clue.text: Baffled hounds bark for water guarded by Labrador

indicators.note: baffled means confused, so the letters of hounds are mixed up

parts.note: to bay is to bark, as hounds do

explanation.surface: Confused hounds bark at the sea beside a Labrador dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Labrador here is the Canadian region bordering the bay, not the dog breed the hounds suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hudson Bay is a large inland sea in Canada, with the Labrador peninsula on its eastern shore.

clue.text: Got the best of the material

explanation.surface: Someone got the finest of the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To have worsted an opponent is to have defeated them; worsted is also a woollen cloth.

clue.text: Oddly nervous about the last letter that turned up, making an appointment

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next piece
oddly means in a strange way, so the letters of nervous are rearranged
in a down entry turning up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: zed is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone nervous about a final letter that arrived is making an appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ZED (the alphabet's last letter) to DEZ; 'about' puts RENVOUS, the anagram of nervous signalled by 'Oddly', around it, with DEZ after REN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendezvous is an arranged meeting at a set time and place.

clue.text: A worker interrupted by ecstatic non-worker

indicators.note: the pair 'a worker' is broken into by the word for ecstatic, which sits in its middle

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
sent is old slang for thrilled or carried away, ecstatic

explanation.surface: A labourer is interrupted by a jubilant shirker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays away from work is absent rather than working, hence a non-worker.

clue.text: Woman lived — you can hear the pulse

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman

indicators.note: something you hear is spoken, so the word for lived is taken by sound

parts.note: having lived somewhere is having been there

explanation.surface: A woman lived, and you can hear her heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' here is the edible seed of a legume, not a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible legume seeds, and the broad bean is one example.

clue.text: Terrifying person arises hence

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an ogre is a frightening person

explanation.surface: A frightful person stands up, therefore.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, a synonym of hence.

clue.text: Become dithguibted — and more involved

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed: 'Become dithguibted — and more involved'; the scan prints the same garbled word and the intended first definition is unknown.

clue.text: Standard or less than standard

explanation.surface: A banner, or something below par.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman legions carried an eagle as their standard; in golf an eagle is two strokes under par, the standard score.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle was the emblem borne as a Roman military flag; in golf it is a score two under par.

clue.text: Goddess of the rainbow

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: A deity of the rainbow, apparently Iris.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Iris, the rainbow goddess; the answer is the Greek queen of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Olympian deities, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: Throw into disorder with bursting grenade

indicators.note: a bursting grenade scatters, so the letters of grenade are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: An exploding grenade causes chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle or disarrange something is to throw it out of order.

clue.text: Farewells are said now to be in progress

explanation.surface: Goodbyes are spoken while things are still happening.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words: farewells are said 'on going', at the moment of departure; as one word it means continuing.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewells are spoken at the point of leaving; and something continuing without a break is still in progress.

clue.text: Possible pips here

explanation.surface: A card player muses on what may turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Pips are the spots marking a playing card's value, so they are found on the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something likely to happen is said to be in prospect; and pips are printed on playing cards.

clue.text: Heaven, they say, is an island

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the word for heaven is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the sky is the heavens above

explanation.surface: Someone claims that paradise is an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is a large island off the west coast of Scotland, an example of the class.

clue.text: Deny I'd turn up to break an agreement

indicators.note: the agreement word is broken open so the next piece can sit inside

parts.note: a contract is a binding agreement

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means reading bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: I'd gives the letters ID

explanation.surface: Refuse that I would arrive to breach a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses I'd to DI; 'to break' splits CONTRACT after CONTRA to take it. In a down clue, 'up' naturally signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict a statement is to assert its opposite, to dispute it.

clue.text: Two bases for plague

parts.note: a bed is a base (a foundation layer), and base also means wicked or evil
a bed is a base (a foundation layer), and base also means wicked or evil

explanation.surface: Two foundations are offered as a remedy for an epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bases' is used in two senses: as a noun (a bed or foundation) and as the adjective base, meaning wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil someone is to torment or harass them, to plague them as a verb.

clue.text: Afterwards meeting someone friendly to one side

parts.note: later means afterwards
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Afterwards, meeting a friend off to the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Laterally means sideways, towards the flank.

clue.text: Declare one's back-sliding relation's left out

indicators.note: sliding backwards means the word one is written right to left

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: the letter for left goes out of the relative's name

parts.note: an uncle is a relation

explanation.surface: Admit that a relapsing relative of yours has been excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-sliding' turns ONE into ENO; 'out' removes L from UNCLE, leaving UNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce or state formally is to declare.

clue.text: Creed a nun came round to, putting up with hardship

indicators.note: coming round suggests turning about, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A nun converted to a belief while enduring difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to bear suffering or strain patiently.

clue.text: Young 'un leaves damaged food

indicators.note: the shortened 'un departs from the word young

parts.note: 'un is the letters UN as written
hurt means harmed or damaged

explanation.surface: A youngster walks away from spoilt food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes UN out of YOUNG, leaving YOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt is a fermented milk product, an example of something eaten.

clue.text: Rangers from. here go west after investing money in privatised industry

indicators.note: the go-west part comes after the first piece in the answer
the industry word surrounds the money letter, as if clothing it

parts.note: gas was a British nationalised industry privatised in 1986
L is the abbreviation for pounds, money
go taken as written

explanation.surface: Rangers fans head west after putting cash into a sold-off utility.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is a Scottish football club based in this city. British Gas, once state-owned, was sold off in 1986.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers Football Club is based in Glasgow, so its home city.

clue.text: Saw getting warm?

explanation.surface: A seen thing is becoming warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NOT ICED: something getting warm is no longer covered in ice.
explanation.definitionFit: To have noticed something is to have seen or spotted it; and something not frozen is warming up.

clue.text: A bloomer to frighten a fielder

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate or frighten
slip is a fielding position in cricket, close behind the batsman

explanation.surface: A blunder that alarms a cricket fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake but means a flower; a slip is a close catching position in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow wild flower, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Metal van

explanation.surface: A two-word note about a metal vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The van (vanguard) is the front position, the place of whoever is in the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is the heavy grey metal Pb; and the van, the forefront, is the leading position.

clue.text: Landlady of the Blue Dragon seen in bed

explanation.surface: An innkeeper spotted in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Lupin keeps the Blue Dragon inn in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit; a flower bed is where the plant grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Lupin is the Dickens innkeeper; and the lupin is a tall garden flower grown in borders.

clue.text: Conflict bedevilling American Western Region

indicators.note: bedevilling means throwing into confusion, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dispute is causing trouble across a western region of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bedevilling' rearranges AMERICAN plus W into CRIMEANWA; the 1850s war fought by Britain, France and Turkey against Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War of 1853-56 is a historical example of an armed conflict.

clue.text: Staff employed in cooking

explanation.surface: Staff who work in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a ceremonial staff of office; mace is also a spice made from nutmeg husk.

clue.text: Musicians forbidden to speak

indicators.note: speaking it means taking the word for forbidden by its spoken form

parts.note: banned means forbidden

explanation.surface: Players who are not allowed to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of people playing music together.

clue.text: Ill-mannered person with dog in queue

parts.note: a pig is a greedy or rude person
to dog someone is to follow them closely, to tail them

explanation.surface: A rude person brings a dog into a line of people waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: A queue (old sense) is a plait of hair hanging at the back of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Queue is an older word for a plait of hair worn hanging down the back.

clue.text: It's cold operating in this castle

parts.note: a chill is coldness
a machine that is on is working, operating

explanation.surface: Someone remarks how cold it is working in this fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: The Castle of Chillon stands on Lake Geneva in Switzerland, made famous by Byron's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Chillon is a medieval Swiss fortress on Lake Geneva, an example of a castle.

clue.text: Unfortunately, Don's away at the moment

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome has gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sadly, Don is currently absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means in the present time, these days.

clue.text: Main method of fastening

explanation.surface: The chief way to fix things together.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a principal or chief item; and a staple is a bent wire clip used to fasten papers.
